source.citation: C. Kittel, Introduction to Solid State Physics, 7th ed. (Wiley, 1996), as tabulated in P.-W. Ma and S. L. Dudarev, Phys. Rev. Materials 3, 013605 (2019), Table I (experimental row, footnote b)
source.notes: Verified 2026-07-01 by pypdf extraction of the EUROfusion submitted manuscript (WPMAT-PR(18) 21177): Table I Cr experimental row: Omega0 = 11.94 A^3, a0 = 2.88 A (footnote b = Kittel 7th ed.; Kittel tabulates room-temperature values). COARSER than the other entries (2 decimals; Cr is absent from the Zhang et al. benchmark set). Consistency check: Young et al. (JPCRD 45, 043101 (2016)) fit their Cr DAC data with V0 = 7.230 cm^3/mol, which converts to a0 = (2 x 7.230/6.02214e23 cm^3)^(1/3) = 2.885 A at 300 K.

source.citation: P.-W. Ma and S. L. Dudarev, Phys. Rev. Materials 3, 013605 (2019), Table I (GGA-PBE, magnetic Cr, 2-atom cell)
source.notes: Verified 2026-07-01 by pypdf extraction of the EUROfusion submitted manuscript: Table I Cr computed row: C11 = 448.12, C12 = 62.03, C44 = 102.13 GPa, Omega0 = 11.72 A^3, a0 = 2.862 A. The paper's main functional is GGA-PBE; AM05 rows appear only for the nonmagnetic metals (V, Nb, Mo, Ta, W), so the single Cr computed row is attributed to PBE. Known PBE underestimate vs experiment (2.88 A) for antiferromagnetic Cr.

unresolved.note: Only a 2-decimal Kittel-attributed value (2.88 A) was verifiable (Cr is absent from the Zhang et al. set whose 0 K three-decimal values cover the other 15 metals). The Young et al. DAC-fit conversion gives 2.885 A at 300 K; a precise 0 K-extrapolated diffraction value for Cr remains unresolved.
